compsNote: 4 of the 4 competitors are within 1 km. Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3; executive condos are left out. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (28% to 46% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 11% over a just-completed resale and about 2.5 points more for each year of its age (29 launches against 102 of their resale competitors, this one and the 7 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 2-bed: buy at or below $2,770, walk away above $2,910, this project about $2,514 psf; 3-bed: buy at or below $2,780, walk away above $2,920, this project about $2,476 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $2,780, walk away above $2,920, this project about $2,492 psf. This project's price by unit type is from the developer's caveats. The developer breaks even at about $2,000 psf (EdgeProp's method); launches since 2023 priced on average 27% above break-even, which points to about $2,540 psf.

supply.ring: outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD)
concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 570 homes, about 1,303 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Sora, Tengah Garden Residences); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 249 resales a year. Our test of 33 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD): those with more than 1,817 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 4.0% a year over the past 4 years, against 4.3% for those with fewer (URA caveats). Supply nearby is not a big concern here.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?

61% sold so far. Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS); with many units left, late discounts or deals on slower stacks are possible as the deadline nears, but the best stacks rarely get cheaper.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?
No other land site nearby is waiting to launch, so there is no newer, cheaper launch to wait for here.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
